newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump on poor retail data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump on poor retail data.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell for the sixth consecutive session Friday, dragged down by a drop in retail sales and political uneasiness, traders said.
The blue-chip IPC index fell 31.75 points to 3,288.29. Volume was a modest 65 million shares.

"September retail sales figures were not well received, and dealers are also nervous over what could happen this weekend with the ERIP," said Arturo Lopez, trader at the Arka brokerage, referring to the self-styled guerrilla group that sent a manifesto to several newspapers on Wednesday.
Mexico's National Statistics Institute said retail sales fell 1.8 percent in September, a bigger drop than had been expected. Wholesale sales came in close to expectations.
In the broad market, losers outnumbered gainers, 61 to 22.
"Foreigners sold market heavyweights like Telmex. I think they preferred to be liquid over the weekend or to invest in the NYSE, which is still rallying," Lopez added.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 53.29 points to 6,471.76, its 11th record high this month.

Telmex L series shares fell 18 centavos ($0.02) to 11.78 pesos ($1.49), while its ADRs fell 3/8 to 29-3/4. Traders said Telmex had additional competition from two international IPOs by phone companies this week, Germany's Deutsche Telekom and Venezuela's CANTV.
The leaders list was headed by insurance firm Genseg, up 20 ($0.03) centavos to 2.43 pesos ($0.31).
Technical analysts noted that selling was triggered when the IPC broke support at 3,300 points.
"The market needed a slide to clean away sales positions which were preventing an upward movement," said Jaime Fernandez at the Interacciones brokerage.
"That frightened dealers a little, but I'm still optimistic and feel the bourse will respect the next support at 3,250 points," he said.
The IPC lost 96.84 points, or 2.9 percent, for the week.
